title: Envy as the First Movement of the Claiming Self
reading:
Envy is the very first motion of the proprium. Before the soul has done anything else with what flows through it, it has already begun to envy: that is, to look at what descends from above and to want it for itself, not as gift received but as possession claimed. Envy is the original shape of self-love in the natural mind, the seed-form of every later wickedness.

When the divine humanity goes forth toward the soul, the proprium sees it and is wounded by what it sees. It cannot bear that something so beautiful should not be its own. So it spits its venom onto the outer truth in which the divine humanity comes clothed — staining what was given, slashing and ruining what it cannot possess.

It envies the first image of the Lord's call, the icon revealed from the height above. It looks upon the likeness it has glimpsed, and rather than receiving the likeness as the Lord's, it stamps an imprint of that likeness onto its own flesh, setting the character of what it saw into the natural body and calling that natural body its own begetting. This is the deepest deception of envy: it sees the divine form and produces a counterfeit of it from itself, then mistakes the counterfeit for its own offspring.

A third time it envies the formed man, the rational that has been shaped under permission to be a vessel of light; and from that rational it snatches what was a power given by the Lord, takes it for its own, and begets from it a self-loved double in the flesh.

A fourth time it stretches out its envy against all the firstborn things and the first works of the Lord — against the blessed One who is father of all, against his wood of suffering, against righteousness itself. There is nothing the Lord brings forth that the proprium does not look on with hatred, gathering all its faculties together in the single purpose of its evil heart, working to penetrate every good with its claim.

This is what the disordered natural is at root: envy. This is the wickedness that casts the soul out from the whole kind of the Living One — not some later sin, but the first turn of the heart by which the soul, seeing what is given, refuses to receive it as given and tries instead to make it its own. From this first beginning every other claim flows.
